bull_bear.body: Diligent product-wise ROI monitoring before launch; Funding multi-category expansion while protecting returns; Strategic JV with Hisense to share capex burden for new facilities.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity price volatility (copper, aluminum) exceeding pass-through capabilities; Seasonal demand mismatch for AC; High channel inventory (4-4.5 Mn units) delaying order normalization; Regulatory costs (E-waste, BEE norms) squeezing brand budgets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasizes 'resilience' despite external headwinds; Clear strategic shift from volume-only RAC to balanced high-margin mix; Transparent on cost pass-through mechanics.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Trade payable days dropped drastically in Q3 due to consumption of existing inventory without new procurement (seasonal lull); Normalized payable days are 90-100. Management explicitly states top-2 customer concentration (now 35-40%) is 'ideal' and will not be reduced further, shifting focus to wallet-share expansion via cross-selling rather than dilution.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The Rs 4,700 Mn capex programme is described as "largely funded".
- Leverage stepped up in FY26: gross debt Rs 7,070 Mn (FY25 Rs 3,697 Mn), net debt Rs 6,912 Mn (FY25 Rs 3,555 Mn), net debt/equity 0.72x (FY25 0.37x), against net worth of Rs 9,603 Mn.
- Returns compressed on the enlarged base: RoCE 5.2% in FY26 vs 10.8% in FY25; RoE 0.4% vs 6.0%.
- Working capital absorbed cash: inventory days 161 (FY25: 98), receivable days 68 (50), payable days 138 (91) and cash conversion cycle 91 days (57); net fixed asset turns fell to 2.4x from 3.2x.
- Shareholding as on 30 June 2026: promoters 46.4%, public 34.9%, DII 11.3%, FPI 7.4% — the deck reads promoter holding as "continued alignment" and "institutional ownership (DII + FPI = ~19%)" as "a stable base".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: RAC: Marginal 1% YoY decline (industry degrowth); SDA: +30% YoY (Air fryers, nutri blenders); LDA: +74% YoY (Washing machines, coolers); Components: +61% YoY (PCBs, copper parts, plastic molding for AC, meters, coolers). RAC contribution ~57-60%, targeting 55% by FY28/29.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need to clear 4-4.5 Mn units of old-rated inventory before ramping new production; Facing 8-10% cost inflation. | Voltas Ltd | beneficiary | Med | As a top AC brand, Voltas benefits from EPACK's capacity to rapidly switch to new BEE-rated production once channel inventory clears, though margin pressure exists industry-wide. |
| High dependency on outsourced manufacturing for cost-efficient scale in new categories like washing machines. | Havells India Ltd | beneficiary | Low | Potential beneficiary if EPACK scales SDA/LDA capacity for third parties, though Havells has significant in-house capacity. |
| Rising component costs and need for localized supply chain for PCBs and plastic parts. | Dixon Technologies | beneficiary | Low | Peer beneficiary of the same structural ODM tailwinds, though EPACK's specific component vertical integration creates a competitive dynamic. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Self-described as "Leading RAC ODM", "Largest Induction Cooktop ODM/OEM" and "Leading Air-Fryer ODM", with a diversified portfolio spanning RAC, LDA, SDA and Components.
- Scale markers on the 'at a glance' page: Total Income FY26 of Rs 19,107 Mn, 72+ trusted customers, 19 product categories, 5 manufacturing locations, 3 NABL-certified R&D labs and '2 decades+' industry experience.
- Stated ambition to "Position EPACK as a strategic single-source manufacturing partner across multiple product categories, enabling deeper customer integration and long-term business partnerships."
- Customer de-risking: top-2 customer concentration fell from 72% of revenue in FY23 to 38%, which the deck calls "materially de-risking the revenue base" (FY26 read 37%; the deck attributes the Q1 FY27 uptick to the RAC-heavy seasonal quarter).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [PLI] The Company has not accrued any PLI income during Q1 FY27, whereas it had accrued PLI income of Rs 133 Mn during Q1 FY26 — the deck footnotes this against its revenue, EBITDA and PBT figures.
- [JV] EPAVO (Bhiwadi) is a JV within the five-plant footprint; the consolidated share of JV loss widened each year — Rs (8) Mn FY23, Rs (15) Mn FY24, Rs (30) Mn FY25, Rs (65) Mn FY26.
- [Margin narrative] The deck frames the current margin pressure as "a sector-wide theme this quarter" and sets the near-term priority as "translating record scale into profitability".
- [Market] Stock data as on 30 June 2026: CMP Rs 230.81, 52-week high/low Rs 414.7 / 196.0, market cap Rs 22,210 Mn, 96 Mn shares outstanding, average volume 1,841k; the deck says the stock "underperformed the Sensex over FY26, tracking the earnings pressure across the RAC sector - a re-rating opportunity if margins and returns recover."
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margins: RAC ~14-15%; SDA/LDA/Components ~16-18%. Cost Headwinds: 8-10% price hike required (50% BEE re-rating, 50% commodity lag from Oct-Dec); Commodity pass-through mechanism protects absolute margins but may compress % margins if base prices rise significantly.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: AC segment 25-30% CAGR to 2030; Industry AC growth 15-20% in CY26; Margin: Targeting 7.5-8% EBITDA medium-term; Order Inflow: Strong RFQs for new BEE-rated products; Capex: INR 450 Cr planned over 12-18 months (INR 218 Cr spent in 9M FY26, INR 225 Cr remaining).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Described as 'very robust' with brands planning 15-20% growth over FY25 numbers; Current production ramping for new BEE-rated units; Inventory liquidation of old-rated stock (4-4.5 Mn units in channel) expected to normalize by end-Q4 FY26, triggering fresh manufacturing orders.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Washing machine vertical (fully auto top/front load) ramping with new MNC customers; Hisense JV commencing production Q4 FY26 (RAC, then WM/TV); Component segment expanding beyond AC to electrical meters and audio; New SDA launches (vacuum cleaners, tower fans) in Q4 FY26.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: EPACK delivered resilient Q3 growth (13.5% YoY) with margin expansion (7.41%) driven by a 74% surge in LDA and 61% in Components, successfully offsetting a marginal RAC decline. The strategic pivot away from RAC dependency (now ~57-60%) toward higher-margin SDA, LDA, and components is de-risking the model ahead of a projected 15-20% industry recovery in CY26 driven by new BEE norms.
